questions.prompt: Directions: Suppose your school is organizing an orientation program to help the freshmen adapt to the new environment and academic studies. You are now to write a proposal, which may include its aim, duration, participants and activities. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
A Proposal for a Freshman Orientation Program

I propose a three-day orientation program to help freshmen understand campus life and prepare for university study. It should take place before regular classes begin and involve new students, volunteer mentors and academic advisers.

On the first day, mentors could guide small groups around the library, classrooms and student service center. The second day should focus on academic skills, including planning study time, finding reliable information and asking for help. On the final day, student clubs could introduce their activities, followed by a discussion about respectful communication and shared living spaces.

Each group should have a clear contact person so that quieter students can ask questions comfortably. A short feedback form would help organizers improve the program. This arrangement combines practical information with personal support, enabling freshmen to begin their studies with confidence rather than feeling lost in an unfamiliar environment.

questions.hint: 提案写目的、时长、参与者与分天活动，不写成已举行的报道。
questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。三天安排对应校园熟悉、学术准备和社交融入；could、should适合建议语气，日期和方案为原创示例。

提案要包含目标、持续时间、参与者和活动：范文先说明帮助新生适应，再把三天分别安排为校园熟悉、学业准备和交流。orientation program是新生适应活动，academic support是学业支持。We propose与could可自然地表达建议；具体日期与人数可另设。检查每项活动对应一个适应问题，不要只报道已办过的活动。结尾可收集反馈，使计划的效果能够评估。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约148词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——提案写目的、时长、参与者与分天活动，不写成已举行的报道。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: Some career women who aim high tend to feel guilty if they fail to achieve their goals.
questions.passage:
There's a stress gap between men and women

A) "I used to work very hard. I love to create things, grow them and solve problems," said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco. "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike."

B) Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness. When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up. "After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself," she said.

C) It's a common story—one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem. Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior. The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels. Clearly, a stress gap exists.

D) "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles. "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." 大运河 (Grand Canal) 是世界上最长的人工河，北起北京，南至杭州。它是中国历史上最宏伟的工程之一。大运河始建于公元前4世纪，公元13世纪末建成。修建之初是为了运输粮食，后来也用于运输其他商品。大运河沿线区域逐渐发展成为中国的工商业中心。长久以来，大运河对中国的经济发展发挥了重要作用，有力地促进了南北地区之间的人员往来和文化交流。
questions.correctAnswer: The Grand Canal is the world's longest artificial waterway, stretching from Beijing in the north to Hangzhou in the south. It is one of the greatest projects in Chinese history. Construction began in the fourth century BC and was completed at the end of the thirteenth century AD. Originally built to transport grain, it was later also used to carry other goods. Areas along the canal gradually developed into China's centers of industry and commerce. For a long time, the Grand Canal has played an important role in China's economic development, greatly promoting travel and cultural exchanges between the northern and southern regions.
